papers.title: Lomb--Scargle Spectroscopy of Non-Polar Interface Traps Governing Anomalous PBTI in GaN FinFETs
papers.summary: In this letter, a spectroscopic framework based on the Lomb-Scargle periodogram is proposed to resolve multi-interface trapping dynamics in GaN FinFETs under positive bias temperature instability (PBTI) stress. Unlike conventional Fourier analysis and discrete multi-exponential fitting, this approach exploits an orthogonal sinusoidal basis for non-uniformly sampled V TH transients, providing a relaxation-frequency representation from which the relaxation-time distribution can be inferred through frequency-to-timescale mapping and physical validation without predefined trapping components. Combined with a facet-de-embedding strategy, the framework isolates the non-polar sidewall-related contribution, whose subsequent Arrhenius analysis reveals a broadened trap-energy distribution centered at 0.54 eV, corroborated by independent DLTS measurements. Furthermore, the extracted power spectrum serves as a weighting function in a dual-channel convolution model, quantitatively reproducing the anomalous temperature-dependent $\Delta $ V TH crossover via the redistribution of trapping contributions across different characteristic time constants. This frequency-domain framework provides a complementary tool for trap-dynamics analysis in multi-gate GaN devices.

papers.title: Synergistic Coupling Effects of Out-of-Plane and In-Plane Polarization in α -In 2 Se 3 Ferroelectric Semiconductor Field-Effect Transistor
papers.summary: The coupling effects of out-of-plane (OOP) and in-plane (IP) polarization in two-dimensional $\alpha $ -In 2 Se 3 based ferroelectric semiconductor-field effect transistor (FeS-FET) are revealed based on TCAD simulation. It is found that single-directional OOP or IP polarization cannot effectively modulate the device state. In contrast, the coupled OOP and IP polarizations significantly regulate the electric field and carrier distribution within FeS channel, endowing a large memory window and a high on/off ratio, which can be attributed to the synergistic enhancement effect of coupled OOP/IP polarization. These results give new insights into operation mechanism and optimization design of FeS-FET as novel ferroelectric memory.

papers.title: 1.6-GW/cm <sup>2</sup> Baliga’s Figure-of-Merit Au-Free p-GaN Gate HEMTs on 6-in Si Enabled by Regrown Ohmic Contacts
papers.summary: High-performance p-GaN/AlGaN/GaN high electron mobility transistors (HEMTs) on 6-inch Si were demonstrated using a CMOS-compatible, Au-free ohmic scheme. Selective MOCVD regrowth of heavily Si-doped n + -InGaN yielded an excellent low wafer-level average contact resistance (R ${}_{\text {c}}\text {)}$ of $0.14~\Omega \cdot $ mm. The integration of regrown ohmic contacts with a dual field-plate architecture, comprising lateral and vertical components, effectively redistributed the electric field and enhanced breakdown performance. For devices with a $15~\mu $ m gate–drain spacing, a threshold voltage of 1 V, a saturation drain current of 465 mA/mm, and an on-resistance (R ${}_{\text {on}}\text {)}$ of $7.2~\Omega \cdot $ mm were achieved, along with an off-state breakdown voltage of 1620 V. These metrics correspond to a Baliga’s figure of merit of 1.6 GW/cm 2 , indicating competitive performance among GaN-on-Si p-GaN HEMTs. Across the 6-inch wafer, both contact resistance and channel sheet resistance exhibited tight distributions, underscoring the manufacturability and process uniformity of the Au-free approach within Si CMOS production lines. This scalable, contamination-free process provides a practical pathway toward high-volume production of GaN power devices with robust electrical performance and CMOS fab compatibility.

papers.title: A Surrogate-Assisted TCAD Modeling Framework for 4H-SiC/SiO <sub>2</sub> Interface in 4H-SiC MOSFET
papers.summary: A surrogate-assisted TCAD modeling framework is proposed for the physics-based extraction of microscopic SiC/SiO 2 interface properties in 4H-SiC MOSFETs. The framework incorporates interface charges, defect-state distributions, and carrier-scattering mechanisms, while a neural-network surrogate and an improved genetic algorithm enable efficient extraction of coupled interface parameters from device electrical characteristics. Compared with the conventional genetic algorithm and full TCAD-based genetic-algorithm optimization, the proposed framework achieves a $16.6\times $ speedup in parameter extraction while enabling quantitative identification of process-dependent microscopic interface properties. The extracted parameters reproduce the measured characteristics of devices with different gate oxidation processes, enabling quantitative comparison of process-dependent interface properties and linking gate-oxide processes to microscopic interface characteristics and device behavior.

papers.title: Electric-field redistribution via high- k dielectric trench in GaN-on-Si AlGaN/GaN HEMTs
papers.summary: We report a GaN-on-Si AlGaN/GaN high-electron-mobility transistor (HEMT) incorporating a drain-side Pb(Zr,Ti)O3 (PZT) trench for electrostatic field management. The mechanism is formulated using the displacement-field boundary conditions and evaluated by two-dimensional technology computer aided design with a field-independent relative-permittivity sweep from 3.9 to 500. The calculations reveal the nonmonotonic dependence of terminal voltage on permittivity and a broader drain-side high-field distribution for the nominal εr=300 case. Experimentally, a representative PZT-trench HEMT reaches 1405 V at LGD=9 μm, compared with 783 V for a co-fabricated conventional device and 957 V for a previously reported hybrid Schottky–ohmic drain HEMT, corresponding to breakdown-voltage improvements of 79% and 47%, respectively, while retaining a specific ON-resistance of 1.47 mΩ cm2. The dynamic-to-static ON-resistance ratios, RON,dyn/RON,static, are 1.6× and 2.5× after 900 and 1200 V off-state stress, respectively, at a 3 μs extraction delay. These results demonstrate simultaneous enhancement of voltage handling and dynamic performance through drain-side dielectric-boundary engineering.

papers.title: GaN Metatransistors for Efficient Sub-THz Power Amplification
papers.summary: This work introduces the concept of metatransistors, which decouples the DC and RF access resistances of a transistor to enable efficient sub-THz power amplification. The device integrates patterned Schottky contacts, coupled to the 2DEG through an ultra-thin insulating barrier, forming a metal-insulator-2DEG metastructure. This structure supports slow waves that confine the RF current injection near the gate as the frequency increases, reducing the RF access resistance ( ${R}_{\text {acc, {RF}}}$ ) while leaving the DC access resistance ( ${R}_{\text {acc, {DC}}}$ ) — and thus the bias current — unaffected. Increasing the number of fingers further enhances this confinement through their collective interaction, compensating for the gate-resistance penalty of periphery scaling. Fabricated metatransistors exhibited up to $50\times $ -smaller ${R}_{\text {acc, {RF}}}$ than ${R}_{\text {acc, {DC}}}$ and an ultra-low RF contact resistance of $0.02~\Omega \cdot $ mm, remaining flat above 150 GHz, and achieved ${f}_{\text {MAX}}$ of 285 GHz while dissipating 51% less DC current than the reference HEMT at the same bias voltages. Load-pull measurements at 160 GHz yielded a peak output power of 0.95 W/mm and a peak PAE of 15.1% — a 68% improvement over the reference HEMT. These results establish metatransistors as a promising route toward ultra-low RF contact resistance and efficient mmWave/sub-THz power amplification.

papers.title: P-GaN Gate HEMTs With Trench-Schottky Hybrid Gate Contact for Enhanced V <sub>TH</sub> Stability
papers.summary: In this work, a trench-Schottky hybrid gate contact design is proposed to improve the stability of threshold voltage ( ${V}_{\text {TH}}\text {)}$ and to modulate the gate leakage of the high electron mobility transistor with p-type-GaN gate cap (p-GaN gate HEMT). This novel hybrid gate contact design includes a partial Ohmic gate contact region, enabling hole injection from the Ohmic gate to compensate for trapped negative charges, thereby improving the ${V}_{\text {TH}}$ stability. Meanwhile, the trench-Schottky structure forms two back-to-back symmetric “L”-shaped depletion regions embedded within the p-GaN layer that effectively narrows the leakage path, thereby suppressing gate leakage introduced by the Ohmic gate contact. Experimental results show that the fabricated device maintains static electrical characteristics comparable to a conventional p-GaN gate HEMT. However, the ${V}_{\text {TH}}$ shift under dynamic gate bias stress is reduced by 87.5% (from 0.4 V to 0.05 V); while the reduction under drain bias stress reaches 58.3% (from 0.72 V to 0.30 V).

papers.title: A Simple Method to Extract the Field Effect Mobility of Free Carriers in SiC MOSFETs
papers.summary: The observed low mobility in SiC MOSFETs is thought to be due to a high density of defects at or above the conduction band edge. Charge trapping in these defects greatly complicates conventional electrical analyses. In this work, we detail a simple analysis to quantify the charge trapping as modification to the threshold voltage. Accounting for this charge trapping allows for an extraction of field effect mobility of free carriers in the channel.
